title.en: Istanbul

overview: Rewind history and delve into the famous battles at Troy and Gallipoli during this 2-day small-group guided tour from Istanbul. Journey to Gallipoli and step on the famous battlegrounds where Turkish troops and the Australia and New Zealand Army Corps (ANZAC) fought to a fatal standoff during World War I. That evening, enjoy staying at a luxurious overnight hotel in Çanakkale. On day 2, you will travel to historic Troy to see where the Trojan War and storied wooden Trojan horse was used to infiltrate Troy’s defenses. With plenty of attention from your guide, round-trip transfer from Istanbul and three meals included this experience can’t be beat. Since this small-group tour is limited to 14 people, enjoy personal attention from your guide.
highlights: 2-day tour to Gallipoli and Troy from Istanbul, including round-trip transport
See the poignant battlefields of the Gallipoli Peninsula, the scene of one of WWI’s bloodiest campaigns
Stand at ANZAC Cove, where Australian and New Zealand forces landed on 25th
Visit ancient Troy to see its crumbled relics and replica wooden horse
Enjoy one night’s hotel accommodation in Çanakkale, and three included meals
Small-group tour limited to 14 people ensures a personalized experience
expect: Your 2-day guided voyage to Gallipoli and Troy is simple with transfers to and from Istanbul. Early on day one, embark by air-conditioned coach to Gallipoli for a tour and complimentary lunch. In the evening, head to neighboring Çanakkale for dinner and your 5-star hotel accommodation (both included). On day two, your hotel provides breakfast and then you will venture to historic Troy. After lunch (own expense), you will have leisure time to explore Çanakkale before heading back to Istanbul that night.

Your tour includes round-trip transport from Istanbul, together with a tour of Gallipoli on day one and an included dinner and one night's accommodation at a 5-star hotel in nearby Çanakkale. On day two, your tour includes breakfast at your hotel, an excursion to ancient Troy, and an afternoon free in Çanakkale before your return to Istanbul in the evening. You won't want to miss this unforgettable historic trip Itinerary
Day 1: Istanbul – Gallipoli – Çanakkale (L, D)

Leave your hotel on the European side of Istanbul in an air-conditioned coach, and travel toward the Gallipoli Peninsula, the scene of one of WWI’s bloodiest military campaigns. Your pickup time is early, so enjoy breakfast (own expense) during a brief stop just outside the city.

Visit the main battle sites and memorials as your guide explains the terrible events that marked the campaign. See the Turkish and Allied trenches at Johnston’s Jolly and view The Nek, a mountain ridge that presided over a tragic Australian attack. Stand at ANZAC Cove, the beach that saw the first landings, and pay your respects at the Australian Lone Pine Cemetery and Memorial, the latter inscribed with the names of almost 5,000 soldiers without a grave. You'll also visit the New Zealand Memorial at Chunuk Blair, the site of a heroic stand by New Zealander troops.
During your tour, take a break for an included lunch at a local restaurant. Then, when your tour ends, travel to your hotel in nearby Çanakkale for an included dinner and the evening at leisure.
Overnight: 5-star Kolin hotel in central Çanakkale or similar
Day 2: Çanakkale – Troy – Istanbul (B)
After breakfast at your hotel, set off by coach on your excursion to ancient Troy, roughly 30 minutes away by road.

Wreathed in legend, this UNESCO-listed archaeological gem is the location of ancient Troy, a city that many scholars believed, until its discovery in 1793, to have been dreamt up by the poet Homer for the purposes of his great work, The Iliad. The city is best known for the Trojan War of the 13th or 12th century BC, when after a 10-year siege by Greek forces, it fell into their hands after they smuggled soldiers inside its walls hidden within a giant, wooden horse.

Gaze in wonder at the crumbled walls and relics as your guide recounts the city's history, including the Greek myth of the Trojan prince (Paris) whose flight with Zeus’ daughter (Helen) triggered the war. You’ll also see the huge, replica wooden horse that stands here to commemorate the city's infamous past.

After your explorations, return to Çanakkale and spend the afternoon as you wish. Perhaps have lunch (own expense) at one of the many enticing restaurants, explore the town's other sights, or shop for souvenirs.
At around 6pm, board your coach and drive back to Istanbul, where your tour concludes with a hotel drop-off in the late evening.

title.en: 3-Day Cappadocia and Ephesus Tour from Istanbul with Flights

overview: Maximize your travel time in Turkey on this 3-day tour that covers Cappadocia and Ephesus, with flights. Turkey is a big country, packed with many diverse regions, which makes it a compelling place to see but also lends to logistical constraints. This tour will ensure you don’t waste any time. First, fly to Kayseri from Istanbul, where you will explore some of Cappadocia’s main points of interest during two tours. Next, fly to Izmir and discover fascinating archeology. Enjoy 4-star accommodations. Select to upgrade your tour if you would like the tour to include your return flight to Istanbul.
highlights: 3-day Turkey tour to Cappadocia and Ephesus from Istanbul
Save time on traveling between regions with domestic flights included
Tour Cappadocia and visit UNESCO-listed Göreme Open-Air Museum, Ortahisar
Castle, Kaymakli Underground City and more
Take an early morning hot air balloon ride over Cappadocia, if you wish Explore the archeological site at Ephesus and visit the House of the Virgin Mary (Meryemana)
Enjoy overnight 4-star stays in a boutique cave hotel in
Cappadocia and a centrally located hotel in Izmir
Upgrade to include a flight from Izmir to Istanbul at the end of the tour
expect: Your 3-day tour kicks off with a flight from Istanbul to Kayseri. Head into the moonscape of Cappadocia, for a great introduction to this otherworldly region. Millions of years ago volcanic ash spewed into the atmosphere, only to fall and cover the earth with layers of ash that solidified. It was then carved out by wind, floodwater, and rain to form the lunar-like landscape you see today.

See the Göreme Open-Air Museum, Kaymakli Underground City, the Rose Valley and select an additional option for a sunrise hot air balloon tour. After seeing Cappadocia’s highlights, traveling to Ephesus where you will steep in Turkey’s very old history. In Cappadocia, enjoy a 4-star boutique cave hotel. In Izmir, a city often cited as the gateway to Ephesus, you will reside in a centrally located 4-star hotel. Itinerary
Day 1: Istanbul – Kayseri – Cappadocia (D)

Start your tour with a hotel pickup from central Istanbul and travel to Atatürk Airport in time for your flight. Board the plane on your own, and relax on the 1.5-hour flight southeast to Kayseri, a city deep in mainland Turkey. On arrival, meet your guide, hop inside your minibus and travel a little further into Cappadocia to see its wondrous sights. Your first stop is Göreme Open-Air Museum, a UNESCO World Heritage site, home to fairy chimneys and a collection of rocky monuments that attest to Byzantine days in Cappadocia. Explore with your guide, and then continue to the small town of Avanos, which is famous for its pottery production.

After a quick look around the pretty town, enjoy a stop nearby in Pasabag (Monk’s Valley), and take a walk through the area’s cone-like rocks to see where monks and hermits once lived in isolated seclusion. Continue traveling through Dervent Valley, where fairy chimneys pepper the landscape, and then travel back to your cave hotel in Cappadocia in time for dinner.
Overnight: 4-star Dilek Kaya Cave Hotel or Alfina Cave Hotel in Cappadocia
Day 2: Cappadocia – Kayseri – Izmir (B, D)

Spend the morning at leisure and enjoy breakfast in your hotel, meet back up mid-morning for another tour of Cappadocia. Start with a walk through Rose Valley, a gorgeous stretch of land that takes its name from its abundance of red-hued rock. Straddling the villages of Göreme and Çavuşin, the valley is peppered with rock-carved churches and tunnels, and your guide will point out the best ones as you walk. Finish up in Çavuşin and, after seeing its cave mosque, enjoy some free time for lunch (own expense).

Hop aboard your minibus and continue your day’s tour to the town of Ortahisar to see its crowning glory, Ortahisar Castle. Pose for photos by the unique rock fortress before traveling onward to the Kaymakli Underground City, one of Cappadocia’s best-preserved subterranean sites. Explore its maze of passages, seeing underground stables and cellars while learning about the early Christians who once hid here to escape persecution. Return to your coach, pass through Pigeon Valley, and then return to your hotel.

Check out in the late afternoon, and travel with your guide to Kayseri Airport for your 1.5- hour evening flight to Izmir. Arrive at Izmir Adnan Menderes Airport on your own, and enjoy a transfer to your hotel. Refuel with a late-evening meal of sandwiches laid on by the hotel and enjoy a good night’s sleep in readiness for tomorrow.
Overnight: 4-star hotel in Izmir
Day 3: Izmir – Ephesus – Izmir (B)

Enjoy breakfast in your hotel, and then travel to Ephesus where an important archeological site, considered as one of Europe’s best-preserved Classical cities, awaits. Explore the ruins on a walking tour and see sights such as the Temple of Hadrian — a monument built to celebrate the Emperor Hadrian’s visits to the city.

Take a break for lunch in the main town (own expense), before traveling to the House of the Virgin Mary, a site that many believe is where the Virgin Mary spent her final days. Enjoy a look around the chapel and hear about its history as a place of pilgrimage from your guide. Finally, return to your coach and travel back to your hotel to check out. Your 3-day tour then finishes with a drop-off at the Izmir airport,Izmir hotel or Kusadasi hotel. Alternatively, upgrade to include a flight back to Atatürk Airport in Istanbul, and finish your tour there instead.

title.en: 6-Day Small-Group Turkey Tour from Istanbul: Pamukkale, Cappadocia, Ephesus and Hierapolis

overview: Discover impressive history and landscape of Turkey's north Aegean region and Cappadocia on this 6-day tour from Istanbul. Step back in time and learn how Greco-Roman history influenced Turkey in Hierapolis and Ephesus. Admire the stunning travertine rock plateaus creating one of Turkey’s most famous natural wonders at Pamukkale. You will visit Cappadocia and see bizarre yet fascinating geology in Çavuşin, Göreme, Uçhisar and more. Enjoy the simplicity of this trip with three domestic flights included (Istanbul to Izmir, Kusadasi to Kayseri and Kayseri to Istanbul). Plus, five nights of lodging and airport rides are included, so your trip is worry-free. This small-group tour is limited to 14 people allowing you more intimate experience with your guide.
highlights: 6-day Turkey tour from Istanbul to Kusadasi, Ephesus, Pamukkale and Cappadocia
Visit Ephesus and see the House of the Virgin Mary and Temple of Artemis
See Pamukkale’s white travertine rock terraces on a tour of the UNESCO-listed archeological site

expect: Your 6-day tour of Turkey begins with a pick-up from your Istanbul hotel and a comfortable transfer to Istanbul’s Ataturk international airport. If you are arriving by plane to Ataturk Airport, simply meet your guide directly at the airport. During your tour enjoy three complimentary domestic flights and five evenings at 4- or 5-star hotel lodgings. Spend a pair of nights in Kusadasi, one evening in Pamukkale, and your last two nights in Cappadocia. All hotels are located within the city center, so you can easily access extra venues and establishments on your own.
Itinerary
Day 1: Istanbul – Ephesus (L, D)

On arrival at Ataturk Airport, board your plane and fly to Izmir at 7.30am. From here, the journey to the ancient city of Ephesus is only 1.5 hours, and you’ll follow a picturesque route along Aegean coastal roads.

Stop for lunch in a traditional Turkish restaurant and then arrive in Ephesus to discover what life was like for the Turks in Greco-Roman times. On a guided tour around the beautifully preserved Classical ruins, see one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World – the Temple of Artemis -- as well as the House of the Virgin Mary, where Mary is said to have spent her final days. See traditional handicrafts being made in town and than head to the nearby town of Kusadasi and check in to your hotel in time for dinner.
Overnight: 4-star Ilayda Avantgarde Hotel or similar in Kusadasi
Day 2: Kusadasi – Pamukkale and Hierapolis (B, L, D)

After breakfast, check out of your hotel and visit a famous leather factory in Kusadasi called Emelda Leather. Turkey is one of the world’s leading producers and exporters of leather goods, and Emelda showcases some of Kusadasi’s finest leatherwork. Browse the locally handcrafted goods with your guide, and shop for quality souvenirs. Enjoy lunch in town and then head to the archeological site of Pamukkale by minibus to see its captivating white travertine rock terraces that cascade down from the ancient city of Hierapolis. While walking around this UNESCO World Heritage Site with your guide, learn about the rock’s geology, and then visit the ancient city of Hierapolis for a dip in its naturally formed bathing pools (own expense). Walk around its majestic ruins, admiring its necropolis (Roman burial site) and vast Roman theater before checking in to your Pamukkale hotel. Enjoy dinner here and then spend the remainder of your evening at leisure. Overnight: 4-star Ilayda Avantgarde Hotel or similar in Kusadasi
Day 3: Kusadasi – Cappadocia (B)

Enjoy breakfast and then leave your hotel by minibus for a transfer to Kusadasi Airport. From here, fly to Kayseri Airport in Cappadocia – Turkey’s stunning central Anatolian region known for its intriguing volcano-created landscape. After a 1.5-hour flight (including an onboard meal) your guide will drive you to your cave hotel. Spend the evening at leisure in beautiful Cappadocia.
Overnight: 4-star MDC Cave Hotel in Cappadocia or a similar standard cave hotel
Day 4: Northern Cappadocia (B, L)

After breakfast, depart by minibus for a full-day tour exploring the north of the region. Stop for a walk around the pretty village of Göreme Esentepe and marvel at its colorful fairy chimneys and lava-formed landscape. The cliff-top village of Uçhisar is nearby, so head here next for a visit to Uçhisar Castle. Enjoy panoramic views from the Byzantine castle’s windows before walking through spectacular Red Valley to the village of Çavuşin for lunch. In the afternoon, hop on board your minibus for a drive to see the Pasabag Fairy Chimneys in Monks Valley – widely considered as the best examples of Cappadocia’s mushroom-shaped rocks. See double- and even triple-headed chimney formations, and then continue your tour through Devrent Valley. Last stop of the day is in Ürgüp for a tour of Turasan Winery, where you’ll sample fine Anatolian wines with your guide. Return to your Cappadocia hotel and spend your evening at leisure.
Day 5: Southern Cappadocia (B, L)

Relax over breakfast and then your guide will collect you for your tour of southern Cappadocia. After a short journey by minibus, arrive in Pigeon Valley to see thousands of sandstone bird houses, carved from the cliffs. Hear about the farmers who for centuries used droppings from the pigeons nesting here to fertilize their crops. Head back to your minibus and make your way to the quaint villages of Selimiye and Yaprakhisar. Several scenes from the Star Wars movies were filmed in Yaprakhisar, and the views from this picturesque cave village are unforgettable. After lunch here, continue your tour to Kaymakli Underground City to see where Turkey’s prehistoric Troglodytes once worked, slept and worshipped.
Day 6: Cappadocia – Istanbul Airport (B)

expect: Day 1 Istanbul - Gallipoli - Canakkale

This morning you will be collected from the lobby of your hotel between 06:00-07:00am. Depart for the 5 hour drive to Gallipoli. Stop for lunch at Eceabat before meeting your guide. This afternoon visit Anzac Cove and the Allied Memorials of World War I, including Brighton Beach, Lone Pine Australian Memorial War Cemetery, the original tunnels and trenches at Johnston Jolly, the Nek Cemetery, and Chunuk-Bair New Zealand Memorial and Cemetery. Cross the strategic straits of the Dardanelles by ferry and continue to Canakkale for overnight.
Day 2 Canakkale - Troy - Gallipoli – Istanbul

This morning visit ancient Troy. As recorded in Homer's "Illiad", the city of Troy was the home of Prince Paris. The excavations undertaken by Heinrich Schlieman in the late 1800’s, and others since, have revealed nine levels of civilisation dating back to 3000BC. Today however, the most obvious landmark is a replica of the wooden Trojan horse. Return to Canakkale and cross the Dardanelles by ferry for lunch at the Eceabat before departing for Gallipoli to visit the Kabatepe Simulation Center. From Gallipoli you will embark on an exclusive boat trip to the landing beaches, which offers the rare opportunity to view the area as the Anzacs saw it during their approach. Highlights of the cruise include viewing from sea Brighton Beach, Anzac Cove and the Anzac Commemorative site. You will also have the chance to snorkel above the sunken wreck of the SS Milo. Return to Eceabat to freshen up before departing at approximately 6:45pm for your return journey to Istanbul. The tour ends on arrival at your Istanbul hotel

On the morning of Day 3, you will journey to Anzac Cove, Lone Pine Cemetery, Gallipoli and other attractions renowned for their historical significance during World War I. After traversing over the Dardanelles, stop in Canakkale for your last night’s accomodation (included).
You last day will be spent reliving the legendary Trojan horse story in Troy. You will have the opportunity to spend some free time after lunch in Canakkale before returning to Istanbul that evening.
Highlights on the tour include:
Topkapi Palace:

This famous Ottoman palace commands a stunning lookout from Seraglio point over the Bosphorus and Golden Horn. Once the throne for sultans, this palace is currently one the world’s largest museums and is filled with an astounding assemblage of Chinese and Japanese porcelain as well as ornate antique jewelry.
Gallipoli:

Learn about the famous battles fought between Turks and ANZAC troops to a deadlock during World War I. Visit Lone Pine Australian Memorial, see Anzac Cove, and reminisce about the loss of life at the trenches and war memorials.
Troy:

This attraction has become popular on the tour as it shows a fantastic recreation of the Trojan Horse and other remnants discovered by the German archeologist Heinrich Schliemann. Plus, listen to the ancient stories of Helen of Troy.

On Tuesdays Topkapi Palace is closed and will be swapped with a visit to Istanbul Archaeology Museum. Grand Bazaar is closed on Sundays, so extra time will be allocated to other attractions. Hagia Sophia is closed on Mondays and will be swapped with a visit to Chora Museum.

Day 01: Istanbul

Your first day is free to beginning exploring Istanbul, Turkey's largest city. The city has long been known for it's strategic location at the entrance of Black Sea and for being the traditional crossroads between Europe and Asia. Depending on your arrival time, you may like to take an optional Bosphorus Cruise. Tonight you have the option of dinner with belly dancing entertainment.
Day 02: Istanbul (B, L)

Today you have a full day of sightseeing in Istanbul. You will visit Topkapi Palace and St Sophie, see the famous Blue Mosque and walk to the Hippodrome, to see the place of the former Horse Ground where chariot races and gladiator fights took place during the Roman Empire time. Today you will end your tour with a visit to the exciting Grand Bazaar with over 4400 shops!
Day 03: Gallipoli - Dardanelles - Cannakkale (L, D)

This morning you have an early departure for Gallipoli to see Anzac Cove, Lone Pine Cemetery and Conkbair with the famous first world war memorials. Cross the Dardanell, which is one of the two waterways between Europe and Asia (approximately 30 minute ferry ride) before arriving in Canakkale around 6:30pm where we will spend the evening.

The morning starts with a visit to Troy, the beautiful city of Helen and the Trojan Horse. Around 12:00pm (noon), return to the Canakkale city for a leisurely free afternoon to enjoy the daily panoramas of a small Turkish Town. For those interested in documentary films such as Gallipoli starring Mel Gibson or 4 Corners Documentary "Fatal Shore" a visit to Anzac House (no charge) may be your choice. At approximately 6:00pm you will depart for Istanbul, arriving back in Istanbul at approximately 11:00pm

Experience three of the highlights of southwest Turkey on a 2- or 3-day tour from Istanbul, with 4-star accommodation in the resort of Kusadasi, one way flights to Izmir, plus airport transfers and all meals included.

With this tour, you're free to choose from a whistlestop 2-day tour and return to Istanbul late on the second day, or to take things easier on a 3-day tour. The latter gives you a second night in Kusadasi, with the chance to relax during the evening and enjoy dinner at your hotel before checking out the next day.

Itinerary Day 1: Istanbul - Ephesus - Şirince - Kusadasi (L, D) After an early morning pickup from your central Istanbul hotel, travel by air-conditioned coach to Istanbul airport for your roughly 45-minute flight to Izmir. On arrival, drive to Ephesus, one of the Mediterranean’s best preserved ancient cities. After about an hour on the road, arrive at Ephesus and enjoy an approximate 2-hour tour of the spectacular ruins. As you stroll the marble-paved streets, listen spellbound as your guide tells the history of the city, once the Roman capital of Asia Minor and home to up to 50,000 people.

See highlights such as the Temple of Hadrian Library of Celsus and Grand Theatre, and step along the Arcadian Way where Cleopatra and Mark Anthony rode in procession in 31 BC. Stroll past age-old shops, houses and see the Roman baths where Ephesians came to relax and socialize.

View the nearby Temple of Artemis, once one of the Seven Wonders of the World, and after a buffet or 3-course Turkish lunch at a local restaurant, visit the House of the Virgin Mary, a stone house built where Mary may have spent her last years.

Lastly, enjoy free time to stroll around the formerly Greek vllage of Şirince, known for its fruit wines. Delve into the cobbled streets lined with craft shops and stalls, and perhaps sample some of the delicious wines. Afterward, travel to your accommodation in Kusadasi and enjoy dinner at your hotel and the evening at leisure.
Overnight: 4-star Ilayda Avantgarde hotel or similar in Kusadasi
Day 2: Kusadasi - Pamukkale – Istanbul (B) or Kusadasi (B)

Leave your hotel after breakfast and after a brief stop at a leather crafts center, continue by coach to Pamukkale, whose name translates as "Cotton Castle" in Turkish. This UNESCO- listed natural wonder consists of a snow-white cliffside of frozen waterfalls and basins, formed when hot springs cascading down the slopes deposited calcium carbonate and hardened into white travertine rock. After admiring the terraces, head to the plateau above Pamukkale to witness the ruins of the city of Hierapolis.

As you explore the site, hear from a guide how it was once a thriving Greco-Roman spa city, where people came to enjoy the hot springs. See the main street, theater and necropolis, and then, if you wish, bathe in Cleopatra’s Pool (own expense) — a hot springs pool strewn with Roman columns.

Your 2-day tour concludes upon arrival back to the hotel. Alternatively, if you’ve selected the 3-day tour, return to your Kusadasi hotel to enjoy evening at your leisure. Overnight if option selected: 4-star Ilayda Avantgarde hotel or similar in Kusadasi Optional
Day 3: Kusadasi (B)
Check out of your hotel after breakfast. Your tour ends in Kusadasi airport.

Itinerary
Day 1: Istanbul - Athens
Begin with a transfer from your European-side Istanbul hotel to Istanbul International Airport. After your 1.5-hour flight, enjoy a transfer from Athens International Airport to your central hotel.

Check in and enjoy some free time to discover Greece’s atmospheric capital. Perhaps shop for souvenirs and ease into Greek culture with a coffee near Syntagma Square, home to the Parliament Building and National Gardens. Later, select from Athens’ many restaurants for dinner (own expense) where you can enjoy local staples such as moussaka (aubergine-and- meat bake).
Overnight: 3-star Hotel Arethusa or similar; 4-star Hotel Athenian Callirhoe or similar; or 5- star Hotel Njv Athens Plaza or similar in Athens
Day 2: Athens (B)
After breakfast, enjoy the day at your leisure. Either look around under your own steam or make the most of your 24-hour hop-on, hop-off bus ticket.

Hop off at any of the 15 stops to experience stellar sights such as the Temple of Zeus, Panathenian Stadium and the Changing of the Guard at Parliament House. Be sure to hop off at the city’s main must-see — the Acropolis of Athens, a UNESCO World Heritage site. Admire its stunning ancient buildings, including the Parthenon, Propylaea gateway and Temple of Athena Nike, and perhaps finish at the nearby Agora, once ancient Athens’ commercial hub.

Learn about Athens' history from the fascinating onboard audio commentary, and perhaps stay on the bus for the full 1.5-hour (red route) circuit for panoramic city views. In the evening maybe head for the district of Plaka – the Old Town – where the lanes buzz with tavernas and bars. Enjoy dinner wherever you choose and perhaps finish at a lively bar or club.
Day 3: Athens (B)
After breakfast, check out and enjoy a transfer to Athens Airport. Return by air to Istanbul, where your trip ends with a transfer to your European-side hotel.

title.en: 4-Days in Romantic Istanbul

overview: One of the most romantic things in Istanbul is definitely being on the water. A good Idea is being on a boat before the sunset and experience all the changes in the sky and watch the bridges and mosques as they light up. Or being on the ferry to the Prince Islands and spending the day walking around, eating ice cream, biking and hopping on one of the horse carriages.
highlights: Enjoy a day away from the hustle and bustle of the city
Explore the local streets on a walking tour of the city
All entrance fees included
Travel by boat and see the sights from the water
expect: Day 1:

Arrival in Istanbul and Evening Sunset Cruise A driver will wait for you at the airport and take you to the hotel. Your 5* Hotel is located in the Heart of the Old City. At 6:15pm you will enjoy a a special evening in Istanbul with this Bosphorus Cruise. Witness breathtaking views over the shining waters of the magnificent Bosphorus. Cruise past the history of the Byzantine and Ottoman Empire, palaces, grand villas and mosques. See the great domes and elegant minarets which grace Istanbul’s skyline. Witness the spectacle of Istanbul’s city lights shimmering across the water from Europe to Asia. Tour Duration: 1.5 Hours
Day 2:

Extensive City Tour Your guide will pick you up at 8am from your Hotel. Today you will discover İstanbul’s top attractions such as the Blue Mosque, Agia Sophia, Basilica Cistern, Topkapi Palace, the Grand Bazaar and the Egyptian Spice Bazaar. After the tour you can either relax in the Hotel, go shopping or visit any of the many museums. Tour Duration: 8 Hours Day 3:

Excursion by boat to Princess Island The Princes’ Islands are a chain of nine rather small islands in the Sea of Marmara. They evolved from a place of exile during the Byzantine era, to a popular destination for tourists and from local Istanbul alike to escape the hectic city life for a day. Of those nine islands, only four of them are open to the public: Büyükada, the biggest and most popular, Burgazada, Heybeliada and Kınalıada. The main feature of any of the Princes’ Islands is the sound of silence. All motorized vehicles are banned, making the islands an oasis of peace and quiet. The only sounds you’ll hear are bicycle bells and the typical sounds of horse hoofs. Yep, that’s right. Horse-drawn carriages and bicycles are the main transportation means on the islands. But that’s not the only feature that makes the Princes’ Islands unique. You’ll find yourself walking or riding through narrow streets flanked by either untouched pine-forests or fine, wooden Victorian cottages. Spend the day walking around, eating ice cream, biking and hopping on one of the horse carriages. The boat ride to the island takes appr. 80 minutes. Tour Duration: 4 Hours Day 4:
According your flight schedule you will transferred back from your Hotel to the Atatürk Airport.

title.en: PRIVATE Western Turkey Tour - 5 Days From Istanbul

overview: You would have chance to visit one of the nicest areas in Turkey, the Aegean, with all it’s historical monuments. Knowing that most of our Australian guests are interested in it, we can also add Gallipoli tour to this program. You will see ancient city of Troy, Pergamon, one of the first hospitals of the world, Asklepion, Ephesus, House of Mother Mary, Artemis Temple which is one of the Seven wonders of the world, Temple of Apollo in Didyma, an ancient roman city, Miletos, a well preserved Greek city, Priene, Aphrodisias, Pamukkale,
highlights: All-inclusive tour
Lunch included
Led by a local guide
expect: ITINERARY:
Day 1 : Istanbul - Gallipoli - Canakkale

After meeting with guide at the hotel, you will have 5 hours driving to Gallipoli where you will visit the battlefield. After Lunch you will visit the war museum, Anzac Cove, The Nek and Lone Pine and Chunuk Bair Memorials. After the tour you will have overnight stay in Canakkale.
Day 2 : Canakkale - Troy - Pergamon - Kusadasi

Departure from hotel after breakfast; Troy is 30min driving distance from Canakkale; you will visit this ancient city, learn about its significance in Greek mythology and in the Trojan War. There is another 3 hours driving to Bergama, where you will have lunch in a local restaurant; after lunch you will get a cable car to the ancient city of Pergamon. While you enjoy the breathtaking view, guide will explain you about the Altar of Zeus, the 2nd largest library of the ancient world, the Temple of Hadrian and the most inclined theater of the ancient world. You will also visit the hospital of Asklepion where Galen, a famous doctor, completed his finest work. After the tour there is 3 more hours driving to Kusadasi; overnight stay.
Day 3: Kusadasi - Ephesus - Kusadasi

Departure from hotel after breakfast and short drive to the ancient city of Ephesus. You will see Odeon, Temple of Domitian, Fountain of Trajan, Terrace Houses Houses, Celsus Library and the largest theater of the Asia Minor. Another site to visit is is the House of Virgin Mary (according to the Catholic church, Virgin Mary lived her last days in Ephesus area). Depending on your interest we can visit some workshops where you can see some handcrafts being done. On the way back to Kusadasi you will visit The temple of Artemis, one of the seven wonders of the ancient World. Overnight stay in Kusadasi.
Day 4: Kusadasi - Priene - Miletos - Didyma - Kusadasi

After breakfast in hotel we will take you to Priene, an ancient city from the 4th century B. C. The temple of Athena, the theatre and the house of Alexander The Great are the highlights of this site. We don’t suggest this tour to guests with walking problem because the city was founded on a steep hill. Another stop is Miletos, where you can see the Faustina Baths and the Theatre. After short drive we will have lunch in Didyma. Afterwards, we will see the Temple of Apollo, the second biggest Greek temple after the one in Delphi. Return to Kusadasi for overnight stay
Day 5: Kusadasi - Aphrodisias - Pamukkale - Istanbul

We will drive 2 hours from Kusadasi. The most interesting points of Aphrodisias, the city of Aphrodite, are the stadium, odeon, monumental gateway and the Temple of Aphrodite. After lunch we will have 1 more hour driving to reach Pamukkale where you will see ancient Hierapolis, the theatre and Necropolis, one of the biggest ancient graveyards. Pamukkale as a miracle of nature famous for it’s white thermal pools. After the tour we will transfer you to the airport for 19:50 Istanbul flight.

overview: Historic Turkey, located at the crossroads of Europe and Asia, combines the history and culture of an ancient land with the development and progress of a modern world. A Turkey vacation with sightseeing tours to Istanbul, or many other destinations, offers the excitement of Turkey’s many cities and archaeological sites, as well as the natural beauty of its colourful landscape.

Your Istanbul stay includes visits to the Hagia Sophia, Hippodrome and the Grand Bazaar, where you receive the famous Evil Eye Turkish amulet as a souvenir gift. Troy and the Anzac World War I cemetery on your way to Kusadasi via Pegamum. Visit and discover the fascinating history of Ephesus. Continue with visits to the fascinating archaeological site of Hierapolis in Pamukkale. Arrive in Konya, and visit the Mevlana Monastery of the Dervishes. title.en: 12-Days Turkey Undiscovered Tour From Istanbul

overview: Turkey has so much to offer the traveller, during their vacation, with its breathtaking natural beauty, unique historical sites and the famous Turkish hospitality. You discover as you step foot on the soil that holds intact remains from the Hittites to the Ottomans and more classical Hellenistic sites than Greece! On this Turkey Undiscovered tour, we visit the WW1 battlefields of Gallipoli, Trojan Horse, and the magnificent acropolis of Pergamum, Ephesus and a visit to the site of the Temple of Artemis, Mediterranean coast, visiting the ancient site of Aphrodisias along the way visit Fethiye, Antalya and Cappadocia with famous fairy chimneys. Highlights
highlights: Small group ensures personal service
All entrance fees included
Perfect introduction for first-time visitors
Breakfast included
What You Can Expect
Day 1Gallipoli Battlefields

Pick up between 6:15 am - 6:45 am from your hotel in the old city of Istanbul or Taksim. We then depart for the Gallipoli Today we visit the WW1 battlefields of Gallipoli including Lone Pine and Chunuk Bair Memorials, ANZAC Cove. Overnight Çanakkale Büyük Truva Hotel (D)
Day 2 Troy, Acropolis of Pergamum
Step back in time today as we visit Troy and its famed Trojan Horse, followed by a tour of the magnificent acropolis of Pergamum. Overnight Kuşadası Suhan 360 (B, D)
Day 3 Ephesus, Kusadasi

Absorb yourself in history today with a guided tour of Ephesus and a visit to the site of the Temple of Artemis, continuing to the former Greek village of Sirince. Carpet weaving has long traditions in Turkey and at the carpet village we learn how the carpets are made by hand and what determines their value. Overnight Kuşadası Suhan 360 (B, D)
Day 4 Pamukkale, Hierapolis

This morning we will enjoy a display of locally handcrafted leather goods before heading to the magnificent white calcium terraces, known as Travertines, in Pamukkale where we also tour the ancient city of Hierapolis. Overnight Pamukkale Colossae Thermal Hotel (B, D)
Day 5 Aphrodisias, Fethiye
Today we drive south towards the Mediterranean coast, visiting the ancient site of Aphrodisias along the way. Overnight Fethiye Marina Vista - Fethiye (B)
Day 6 Fethiye

Today you have the option to relax on a day cruise around the 12 Islands of Fethiye or experience one of Turkey's highlights on an optional day tour to Saklikent Gorge, Turkey's longest and deepest canyon. Overnight Fethiye Marina Vista - Fethiye (B)
Day 7 Kayakoy, Antalya
Relaxing morning, before a late afternoon drive to the resort town of Antalya visiting the deserted Greek village of Kayakoy on the way. Overnight Antalya Best Western Khan Hotel (B, D)
Day 8 Aspendos, Manavgat Waterfalls

Today, we will visit famous theatre at Aspendos which is known for one of the best preserved theatres of Asia Minor, still used today. Then we will visit Manavgat Waterfalls for a pleasant resting spot. Overnight Antalya Best Western Khan Hotel (B, D)
Day 9 Konya, Cappadocia

Early departure for Cappadocia, stopping en-route to visit Konya and the mausoleum of Mevlana Celaleddin Rumi with its accompanying museum. This afternoon we also stop to visit Sultanhani Caravansary, the largest in Anatolia. Overnight Cappadocia in a Cave Hotel (B, D)
Day 10 Goreme, Uchisar Castle
Marvel at the lunar landscape with a fully guided tour of Goreme Valley, the fairy chimneys, Uchisar castle and more. Overnight Cappadocia in Cave Hotel (B, D)
Day 11 Ihlara Valley, Underground City
Today we trek through the wildly beautiful Ihlara Valley and explore the many levels of an underground city. Overnight Cappadocia in a Cave Hotel (B, D)
Day 12 Ankara

Early morning departure to the nation's capital, Ankara, where we visit Anitkabir, mausoleum of the famed Mustafa Kemal Ataturk, before returning to Istanbul. Our tour concludes with the arrival to Istanbul at approximartely 7 pm. (B)

title.en: 3 Day Gallipoli in Depth Tour from Istanbul with Troy

overview: Great for those who are really interested Gallipoli history this 3 day tour will explore the Gallipoli and Troy region in depth from Istanbul. Travel from Istanbul to Gallipoli peninsula where you will spend the afternoon visiting the battlefields including ANZAC cove, Lone Pine Australian Memorial, Johnston's Jolly (Turkish and Allied Trenches) and Chunuk- Bair New Zealand Memorial. The following day a visit to the archaeological and mythical site of Troy is a highlight before lunch visiting the Naval base, Nusrat Mine Layer, Cimenlik Castle and the Naval Museum. Explore the Helles and Suvla sectors of the Gallipoli region before returning to Istanbul.
Highlights
All entrance fees included
Free hotel pickup and drop-off included
Lunch included
Vegetarian meal option available
Led by a local guide
Multi-Day Trip
What You Can Expect
Day 1: Istanbul - Gallipoli - Canakkale

This morning you will be collected from the lobby of your hotel. Depart Istanbul, driving along the north shore of the Sea of Marmara to the Gallipoli Peninsula, arriving at approximately 12:00pm. Lunch at Eceabat Maydos Restaurant & Bar. This afternoon visit Anzac Cove and the Allied Memorials of World War I, including Brighton Beach, Lone Pine Australian Memorial War Cemetery, the original tunnels and trenches at Johnston Jolly, the Nek Cemetery, and Chunuk-Bair New Zealand Memorial and Cemetery. Late this afternoon cross the strategic straits of the Dardanelles by ferry and continue to Canakkale for overnight.
Day 2: Troy & Canakkale

This morning visit ancient Troy. As recorded in Homer's "Illiad", the city of Troy was the home of Prince Paris. The excavations undertaken by Heinrich Schlieman in the late 1800’s, and others since, have revealed nine levels of civilization dating back to 3000BC. Today however, the most obvious landmark is a replica of the wooden Trojan horse. The afternoon return to Cannakale for a tour to visit the Naval Base, Nusrat Mine Layer, Cimenlik Castle and the Naval Museum. Overnight in Cannakale.
Day 3: Canakkale – Istanbul

Further explore the historical Gallipoli battlefields visiting the landing beaches, cemetery, Pink Farm, 12 Tree Copse, Skew Bridge and V-beach at the Helles Sector. Lunch at Eceabat Maydos Restaurant & Bar. After lunch visit the sites of the Suvla sector including Suvla Bay, Scimitar Hill, Embarkation Pier NZ No. 2 Out Post, 7th Field Ambulance Cemetery, Hill 60 Cemetery & NZ Memorial, Green Hill Cemetery, Hill 10 Cemetery and Azmak Cemetery. Depart from Cannakale at approximately 5:45pm with a stop en route for dinner (own expense) before arriving back to your Istanbul hotel at approximately 11:45pm.

expect: Day 1 Tue Istanbul 20kms
Arrival transfer from Istanbul airport to hotel.
Day 2 Wed Istanbul 30 kms

Visit Topkapi Palace, the largest and oldest of the remaining palaces where Ottoman Sultans used to live; admire the gardens, kitchens, the treasury section as well as terraces overlooking the Bosphorus and the Golden Horne. Explore Saint Sophia, one of the marvels of Byzantine architecture. Visit the Blue Mosque covered by more than 20.000 Iznik tiles and the Roman Hippodrome. In the afternoon, discover the handcrafts of Anatolia and shop in the labyrinth tunnels of the Grand Bazaar. Return to the hotel. Overnight. (BL)
Day 3 Thu : Istanbul – Ankara 460 kms

Free time in the historical Spice Market to feel the exotism of the Orient. Enjoy a langourous boat trip along the European and Asian coasts of the Bosphorus. In the afternoon, cross the Bosphorus Bridge and proceed to Ankara. Dinner and overnight in the capital of Turkey. (BD)
Day 4 Fri : Ankara – Cappadocia 310 kms

Visit to Archeological museum of Ankara, with its unique collection including Paleolithic, Neolithic, Hattie, Hittite, Phrygian, Urartian and Roman works and Lydian treasures. Short stop in the Mausoleum of Kemal Ataturk, founder and first president of the Turkish Republic. Proceed to Cappadocia. Visit of an underground city. Check-in to your hotel in Cappadocia, dinner and overnight. (BD)
Day 5 Sat : Cappadocia 80 kms

Entire day to enjoy the natural beauty and the cultural depth of this unique region : explore the frescoed interiors of Goreme's cave churches, which date from the 8th century, take a walk in Avcilar, Pasabagi and the valley of Dervent where you will admire the chimney like volcanic formations. Lunch and a brief photo stop at Uchisar. In the afternoon, discover the unique artifacts of Cappadocia such as pottery, onyx etc. Dinner and overnight. (BLD)
Day 6 Sun : Cappadocia – Konya - Pamukkale 630 kms

Drive through the Silk Road to Konya to visit the Whirling Dervishes Convent which is now the Mevlana Museum. Visit a Caravanserail from XIIth century. Continue to Pamukkale, dinner and overnight. (BD)
Day 7 Mon : Pamukkale - Ephesus - Izmir 290 kms

Discover the ancient city of Hierapolis and enjoy the unique splendor of its cascading, hot springs in Pamukkale. Proceed to Ephesus and explore the antique city by wandering along its 2,000 year old marble streets to such famous sites as the theatre and the Celsus Library. Stop at a leather factory in Selcuk to attend a fashion show and to learn more about Turkish leather. Visit the Home of Mother Mary. Continue to Izmir, third biggest city of Turkey. Dinner and overnight. (BD)
Day 8 Tue : Departure 20 kms
Transfer to Izmir Airport for your onward flight. (B)

title.en: 15-Day Turkey and Greece Tour From Istanbul

overview: Guided coach tour through Turkey and Greece visiting Istanbul, Cappadocia, Pamukkale, Ephesus, Pergamon, Troy, Gallipoli, Athens, Epidauros, Olympia, Delphi and Meteoras. Unique experience in selected hotels crowned by culture and history.
highlights: 15-day tour to iconic and culturally rich locations in Turkey and Greece from Istanbul
Admire dramatic landscapes and historical monuments in Turkish cities like
Cappadocia and Pannukale
Discover the ancient history of intriguing Greek locations like Athens, Olympia and
Delphi
Enjoy 15 nights' accomodation in luxurious 4- or 5-star hotels
Receive selected meals and round-trip transportation by luxury, air-conditioned vehicle throughout the tour
expect: Istanbul 20km
Arrival transfer.
Istanbul

Visit Topkapi Palace, where Ottoman Sultans used to live; Explore Saint Sophia, a marvel of Byzantine architecture,the Blue Mosque covered by more than 20.000 Iznik tiles and the Roman Hippodrome. Shop in the Grand Bazaar.
Istanbul-Cappadocia
Free time in the historical Spice Market. Enjoy a boat trip along the European and Asian coasts of the Bosphorus. Transfer to airport for flight to Kayseri or Nevsehir (not included).
Cappadocia

Explore the frescoed interiors of Goreme's cave churches, take a walk in Avcilar, Pasabagi and the valley of Dervent. Lunch and a brief photo stop at Uchisar. In the afternoon, discover the unique artifacts of Cappadocia such as pottery, onyx etc.
Cappadocia-Pamukkale
Drive through the Silk Road to Konya to visit the Whirling Dervishes Convent which is now the Mevlana Museum. Visit a Caravanserail from XIIth century.
Pamukkale-Izmir
Discover the ancient city of Hierapolis and enjoy the unique splendor of its cascading, hot springs in Pamukkale. Proceed to Ephesus and explore the antique city. Visit the Home of Mother Mary.
Izmir-Canakkale
Proceed to Pergamon, the city where parchment was invented and visit the Acropolis. After lunch, visit the legendary city of Troy, immortalized in Homer’s Iliad.
Canakkale-Istanbul
Cross by ferry the Strait of Dardanelles and discover Gallipoli where the bloodiest battles of First World War took place; visit the Anzac Cove, Lone Pine and Chnuk Bair
Istanbul-Athens
Transfer to airport for your onward flight (not included). Arrival to Athens, transfer to hotel.
Athens

Depart for your Athens Sightseeing tour including the Acropolis, You will see the Hadrian’s Arch, the Temple of Olympian Zeus and the Panathinaikos Stadium and the famous Parthenon. Your first taste of Athens would not be complete without a visit to the Acropolis Museum.
Athens-Olympia

Reach the Corinth Canal. Continue to Epidaurus with its 4th century B.C. theatre, famous for its astonishing acoustics. Visit the town of Nafplion and stop at Mycenae, the Homeric city of Atreides. Depart for Olympia through Central Peloponnese.
Olympia-Delphi

Visit Ancient Olympia. Visit the Sanctuary of Olympian Zeus and the Archaeological Museum of Olympia. Continue through Achaia and Rio Antirio towards Delphi, passing through the picturesque towns of Nafpaktos and Itea.
Delphi-Kalambaka
Depart for Delphi, the home of the Sanctuary of Apollo Pythios. Visit the Treasury of the Athenians and the Delphi Museum.
Kalambaka-Athens
Visit the monasteries of Meteora perched on huge granite rocks.
Transfer to Airport.

title.en: 10 Days Turkey Tour: Istanbul, Cappadocia, Pamukkale, Ephesus and Troy

overview: Visit Turkeys top five must see attractions in 10 days! See the highlights of Istanbul before heading to the volcanic area of Cappadocia. See the beautiful landscape of Pamukkale before learning about the infamous Ephesus and Troy.
highlights: Perfect introduction for first-time visitors
All-inclusive tour
expect: Day 1 - Istanbul- (D)

If arriving at Istanbul Atakurk airport (IST) you will be met and transferred to your starting hotel. If arriving at Sabiha Gokcen Airport (SAW) airport please make your own way to the hotel. As today is an arrival day, there is no formal sightseeing planned.
Day 2 - Istanbul to Cappadocia- (B&L&D)
This morning your guide will introduce you to the treasure-trove of the historic old town. In the late afternoon you will drive to the airport for your flight to Cappadocia.
Day 3 - Cappadocia- (B&L&D)

This morning you will visit the Göreme Open Air museum: The people of Göreme, at the heart of the Cappadocia Region, realized that the soft rocks of the area could be easily carved out to form houses, churches, monasteries.
Day 4 - Cappadocia- (B&L&D)
After a relaxing breakfast you will take a walk toward Kizilcukur (Red Valley), where its magnificently sculptured, red rock formations have created arguably the most beautiful valley in Cappadocia.
Day 5 - Cappadocia - Konya- (B&L&D)

Leaving the fairytale landscapes of Cappadocia behind and driving to the incredible underground city of Derinkuyu. Some of the dwellings here contain rooms expanding seven levels beneath ground level. You will then leave the area of Cappadocia behind and drive to Konya, your stop for the night.
Day 6 - Konya - Pamukkale - (B&L&D)
After breakfast this morning you will drive to Pamukkale, also known as "Cotton Castle" and a truly unique sight. You will spend the night in a hotel in Pamukkale
Day 7 - Pamukkale - Ephesus - Selçuk- (B&L&D)

After breakfast you will make an early start for a drive of about four hours to Selçuk, which will be your base for visiting Ephesus - one of the best-preserved classical cities in the eastern Mediterranean, and a great example of Roman architecture. You will spend the night in a hotel in Selçuk.
Day 8 - Selçuk - Troy - Çanakkale- (B&L&D)

Early this morning after breakfast, you will begin the drive to Çanakkale, located on the shores of the Dardanelles. On the way, you will visit an important historical site near Çanakkale - Troy. Troy (Truva) was a city that existed over 4,000 years ago and was known as a major ancient civilization.
Day 9 - Çanakkale - Gallipoli - Istanbul- (B&L&D)

You will cross the Dardanelles and return to "Europe" today, visiting the Gallipoli Peninsula - a place of enormous significance to Australians and New Zealanders. You will arrive back in Istanbul in the late afternoon or early evening and the remainder of the evening will be free.
Day 10 - End - Istanbul (B)
Your tour will come to an end this morning after breakfast.

expect: On our way to Cappadocia, we fly to Nevsehir or Kayseri airport and drive south to Uchisar in the midst of the Cappadocian heartland, where we will be staying at the luxurious Cappadocia Cave Hotel. Cappadocia is a region unlike any other. Its extraordinary landscape is composed of soft volcanic stone that wind and rain have sculpted into fantastic clusters of multicolored spires and pinnacles. What is more, the softness of the stone encouraged the medieval Christian inhabitants of the region to carve out of the living rock literally hundreds of churches, monasteries, towns and villages. A trip to Cappadocia is a magical experience you will never forget.We will be visiting at one of the regions famous 'underground cities'.We will visit the great rock-hewn citadel that looms over the town. On our second day we will visit the open-air museum of the Goreme Valley, which contains the regions highest concentration of painted churches. The frescoes are among the masterpieces of Byzantine art. A short distance beyond Goreme lie the villages of Avcilar and Cavusin, both of which have many cave-dwellings, and the dramatic Zelve Valley.

Today we tour the Goreme open-air museum, Pasabag and Uchisar castle and Kaymakli underground city. Photo opportunities are everywhere so have your cameras ready! Carpet weaving has long traditions in Turkey and at the carpet village we learn how the carpets are made by hand what determines their value. Tonight, don't miss the optional Turkish folklore evening featuring folklore and belly dancers... a night you won't forget! Overnight Cappadocia Cave Blue Valley Hotel (B, D)

Leaving Cappadocia we head south along the ancient Silk Road just as the ancient traders did. Along the way we visit Sultanhani Caravansary, before stopping at Konya to tour the Mevlana Museum. Overnight Pamukkale 5 star Colossae Thermal Hotel (B, D)

title.en: 81) 3-Day Aegean Myths And Beauty Tour from Istanbul

overview: Aegean sea coast of Turkey inspired mankind to build temples, start wars and fall in love. This beautiful land scape indulges visitors with the dance of turquoise shores and olive trees. In three days you will visit the best spots Aegean coast offers. Troy, Pergamun and Ephesus. Pamukkale will also be included as a highlight on your journey.

expect: The ancient cities in Western Turkey have been the cradle of civilization since the mythological times. This 3-day journey will take you to the focal points of this tremendous cultural heritage. It will be a journey to a land where myth, beauty and history are melted in a golden pot.
DAY 1:

On the first day of your journey, you will visit Troy, the site of the Trojan War and Pergamum, the birthplace of parchment. Your tour will start with an early morning departure from the hotel at 06:00 am. As you cross the Dardanelles by ferry, and drive the last 25 minutes to the site of Troy, you will become a part of Homer’s legends, seeing the symbolic Trojan horse, the city walls, The Athena Temple and the Odeon. Then you will follow the route taken by those who have escaped the fall of Troy, fleeing from the wrath of Agamemnon, to the city of Pergamum.

Pergamum had hosted one of the biggest libraries of ancient ages, before it was destroyed. You will walk through the ages at this site; visiting the Acropolis and the Asklepion, which indeed has been an inspiration, as well as a prototype for the modern healthcare center of our day. Dinner and a overnight stay in one of the best hotels in modern Pergamum.
DAY 2:

The second day of your tour will start with a drive, via the Aegean city of Izmir, to Selcuk area. You will then visit the ancient city of Ephesus, the Roman capital of Asia Minor. Your tour will include the Odeon, the Marble Street, the Hadrian Temple, the Celcius Library and the Great Theatre You may opt for lunch in a local restaurant, before paying a pilgrimage visit to the House of Virgin Mary. This Christian and Muslim shrine is located in the vicinity of Ephesus; and it is believed by many that Virgin Mary, was taken to this stone house by Saint John and lived there.
DAY 3

Pamukkale, meaning "cotton castle" in Turkish, is a natural site that is created by hot springs and travertines, terraces of carbonate minerals left by the flowing water. The ancient city of Hierapolis was built on top of the white "castle" which is nearly 9 thousand feet long and more than 500 feet wide. After an optional lunch, you will drive to another land of dreams; this time to Aphrodisias. The city was especially well – known with the temple dedicated to its protecting Goddess Aphrodite and its sculptors.

Your tour of the ancient city will include the Theater, the Basilica, the Roman Baths; and the biggest stadium of the ancient time. You will also see the museum and its magnificent marble statues. Your car will then take you back to Izmir Airport for the flight to Istanbul. The tour will end with a private transfer to your hotel.

After breakfast, you will leave the hotel to travel to the Cappadocia region. Prepare yourself to travel back in time, and prepare your mind to wander between the images of ancient people and the breath taking beauty of the landscape. The drive to Cappadocia will take you to the shores of the picturesque Salt Lake, a vast ocean of white. The first spot to visit in Cappadocia will be the Ihlara Valley, which was formed by volcanic eruptions; and where the scenery is fascinating. You will then visit the Derinkuyu Underground City, where the early Christians seek refuge as they fled the wrath of none-believers. This long day’s journey will end at Nevsehir, the center of the Cappadocia region; where you will stay for the night. title.en: Discover Cappadocia In 2-Days From Istanbul

overview: Prepare yourself to travel back in time, and prepare your mind to wander between the images of ancient people and the breath taking beauty of the landscape. First day visit to the underground city and Ihlara valley; second day Göreme open air museum, Paşabağ (monks valley) and Imagination valley will be the highlights of your itinerary.
highlights: Ideal choice for families
Small group ensures personal service
Airport transfer

expect: Cappadoccia was an object of desire to men, even before it was mentioned in the Holy Bible. Once the capital of the powerful Hittite empire, later a refuge for early Christians; it is a land of magic, a region of exceptional natural wonders (in particular characterized by fairy chimneys) and a unique historical and cultural heritage. Prepare yourself to travel back in time, and prepare your mind to wander between the images of ancient people and the breath taking beauty of the landscape.

Day 1 Your vehicle will be waiting for you for an early morning transfer to the airport. Following the flight to Kayseri city, you will travel to Cappadoccia region by driving within the escort of the English speaking guide.The first step will be Derinkuyu Underground City which is the biggest of the region with its 12 stations under the ground. On the way to Ihlara Valley, the Crater Lake, Nar Golu, will greet you with its magnificent scenery. Upon arrival at Ihlara Valley, 14 Km long and some places 140m deep with 4000 carved caves, start exploring the deep canyon by walking through the valley (4km). Then reach to Belisırma village for the lunch in a local restaurant. After lunch we drive to end of Ihlara Valley to watch the magnificent view and visit Selime Rock-Cut Monastery. Then leave Ihlara Valley behind and drive to hotel via Selime village.

Day 2 Breakfast will be served at the hotel, before leaving for the Göreme Valley. Turks have a legend that explains the etymology of the name as: “Gör, Emi (see it for sure)”. This is not without a reason, for this is the important site of the region. The valley is home to rock churches and monasteries, going back as much as to 2nd century AD, which are richly decorated with colourful frescoes by exiled Christians in Roman era. The wonders will then continue with the amazing panoramic view that you will enjoy at the natural citadel of Uçhisar. You will witness the poetry, written through the ages on the soft volcanic rock by the no other than the elements of the nature. The wind and the rain have worked together to create a surreal, almost lunar landscape; a scene of pillars and cones and, of course, the unique fairy chimneys.

After having lunch at an authentic restaurant, short walk through out Zelve - Paşabağ where you will find the most interesting fairy chimneys and possible to see the first example of monk’s chapel. Visit to Avanos for traditional handicraft as pottery manufacturing by Hittite technique and Tiles & Plates. Then head to Devrent Valley (Fairy Valley) for a close witness to fairy chimneys. After visit the wine factory and taste of delicious Cappadocian wines, stop for characteristic fairy chimneys in Ürgüp. Then transfer to the Kayseri Airport to fly back to Istanbul and transfer to your hotel.

title.en: 8-Day Turkey and Greece Tour from Istanbul: Greek Islands and Athens Cruise plus Ephesus, Pamukkale and Cappadocia by Bus

overview: Delve into Turkish and Greek life during an 8-day land and cruise tour from Istanbul of Turkey’s marvels and the Greek Aegean islands. Experience the highlights of the Sultanahmet district visiting the Blue Mosque and the Hagia Sophia. Then from Kusadasi, spend four days cruising the best of Greece in Crete, Patmos, Mykonos, Santorini and Athens. Return to Kusadasi for a land expedition to Turkey’s wonders including Ephesus, Cappadocia and Pamukkale. This adventure ends where it started back in Istanbul. Included in this tour is hotel accommodation, coach and transfers, most meals and domestic air fare which makes this a fantastic trip to uncover the beauty and rich history of both countries.
highlights: 8-day cruise and land tour around Turkey and the Greek Aegean islands from Istanbul
Enjoy a 4-day cruise visiting four Greek islands and Athens, on a modern cruise ship
Stop to visit beautiful Patmos, Crete, Santorini and Mykonos, as well as historical
Athens Explore Turkey’s highlights of Ephesus, Pamukkale and Cappadocia by comfortable coach
See Istanbul’s top attractions, including the Hagia Sophia, Blue Mosque and Grand
Bazaar Enjoy 10 included breakfasts, 8 lunches and 9 dinners, plus an included cruise drinks package
Enjoy included 4- and 5-star hotel accommodation and two domestic flights within
Turkey
expect: Your 8-day cruise and land tour kicks off in Istanbul with a visit to Blue Mosque and Hagia Sophia in the Sultanahmet district before meeting your cruise ship in Kusadasi. Next, you will spend four days cruising the Aegean sea to the Greek Islands of Santorini, Crete, Patmos and Mykonos including a stop on Greece’s mainland, Athens. Return to Kusadasi where your cruise ends and continue overland to Turkey’s top attractions such as Pamukkale, Ephesus and Cappadocia before concluding in Istanbul.

Included in this trip is your domestic flights, an air-conditioned coach and professional guide in Turkey, and 4- or 5- star hotels in Pamukkale, Cappadocia, and Istanbul. Also included are 10 breakfasts, eight lunches, and all meals on your cruise ship, the cozy Celestyal Olympia. Plus an on board drinks package is included. Island adventures and tours are at your own expense.
Itinerary
Day 1: Istanbul (D)

Start your experience with an included transfer from either Istanbul’s Atatürk or Sabiha Gokcen International Airport, Istanbul cruise port or your centrally located Istanbul hotel. Then, after checking in at your Istanbul tour hotel, enjoy an optional half-day sightseeing tour (own expense) of this historical city. Standing at the crossroads of Europe and Asia, Istanbul was known as Constantinople between the 4th and 20th centuries and is packed with treasures. If you opt to take the tour, you’ll explore the UNESCO-listed ‘Historic Areas of Istanbul,’ and admire the dazzling Blue Mosque; the Hagia Sophia, the ancient Christian basilica that became a mosque; and the Topkapi Palace, the opulent residence of Ottoman emperors.
After dinner at your hotel, enjoy the evening at leisure.
Overnight: 4-star Vicenza hotel or similar in Istanbul
Day 2: Istanbul – Izmir - Kusadasi – Patmos (B, L, D)

After breakfast, travel to Istanbul Atatürk Airport for your flight to Izmir on Turkey’s Turquoise coast. On arrival, travel to Kusadasi by air-conditioned coach and embark on your 4-day Aegean cruise.

Board your ship in the early afternoon and leave for Patmos, in the Greek Dodecanese archipelago. Known for its picture-postcard looks, Patmos boasts two UNESCO World Heritage sites: the hilltop Monastery of St John, and the Grotto of St John, where the saint reputedly penned the bible's Book of Revelation. After mooring, join an optional excursion (additional cost) to visit these religious sites, with the chance to see the capital of Chora spread beneath the monastery. Afterward, enjoy dinner on board before you sail overnight to Crete.
Overnight: at sea between Patmos and Crete
Day 3: Crete - Santorini (B, L, D)

Arrive at Crete in the early morning, and enjoy breakfast on board. Greece’s largest island, Crete is a fabulous mix of archaeological treasures, bustling towns, brilliant shopping and beautiful beaches.

After docking at the capital, Heraklion, set off to explore the historical highlights of this interesting town at leisure, or choose one of the optional excursions (own expense) on offer, including a trip to the Palace of Knossos.

Excavated in 1898, the partially restored ruins of Knossos date from the 2nd millennium BC and mark out what was once a grandiose palace and the seat of Minoan civilization. Learn how the site was the home of King Minos and the Minotaur — the mythological monster that roamed an underground labyrinth — and as you walk, hear fascinating insights into the Minoan period.

After lunch on ship, sail to Santorini, the breathtaking Greek island that overlooks a semi- submerged volcanic crater (caldera). Explore the capital, Fira, at leisure or enjoy an optional excursion (own expense), perhaps discovering the interior by 4x4, island-hopping in the crater, or visiting the village of Oia for magical sunset views over the caldera. Return to your ship and sail for Athens overnight. Overnight: at sea between Santorini and Athens
Day 4: Athens - Mykonos (B, L, D)

Moor at Athens early and enjoy breakfast as you absorb the views of the Acropolis. Then, join an optional excursion (own expense) to see Athens’ highlights, including the magnificent marble Parthenon that stands on the Acropolis above the bustling city. Around lunchtime, return to your ship and cruise to Mykonos. Peppered with whitewashed towns and windmills, this lovely island is famed for its designer shops, bars and nightlife. Dock at Mykonos Town, and spend the evening as you wish, perhaps shopping at the arty stores or admiring a sunset from a waterfront bar. After dinner on board, cruise overnight to Kusadasi. Overnight: at sea between Mykonos and Kusadasi.
Day 5: Kusadasi – Pamukkale (B, L, D)
Arrive in Kusadasi in the morning, and relax over breakfast, before leaving your ship and ending your cruise.

Then, board an air-conditioned coach and travel to nearby Ephesus, one of the Mediterranean’s greatest classical sites. Explore the well-preserved Greco-Roman ruins of this once-thriving city, and see its showpiece monuments. Admire the majestic Celsus Library and Grand Theater, where St Paul once preached, and walk down the marble streets to see the shells of shops, temples and baths.

After a stop for lunch, continue to Pamukkale or ‘Cotton Castle’ in Turkish. This UNESCO- listed site comprises white travertine rock terraces that cascade down cliffs. Admire the sight as your guide shares facts about the geology behind the terraces. Then, work your way up to the ruined ancient city of Hierapolis perched on the cliff plateau. Wonder at the relics before you, including Roman temples, tombs and thermal pools.
This evening, check in at your hotel.
Overnight: 5-star Spa Hotel Colossae Thermal or similar in Pamukkale
Day 6: Pamukkale – Konya – Cappadocia (B, L, D)

Enjoy an early breakfast and travel by coach to Turkey’s Cappadocia region. During your journey, trace a fascinating stretch of what was the fabled Silk Road and visit one of the kervansarays (caravan palaces) along the route, the Sultanhani Caravansary. Continue to the 800-year-old city of Konya, the birthplace of Turkey’s whirling dervish dance. After a stop for lunch, visit the Mevlana Museum, dedicated to the Muslim poet Mevla Celaddiini-Rum, and travel onward to Cappadocia, arriving in time for dinner. Overnight: 4- star Lykia Lodge Hotel or similar in Cappadocia
Day 7: Cappadocia - Istanbul (B, L, D)

Following breakfast, enjoy a full-day excursion in this beautiful region, where the elements have carved the soft volcanic landscapes into spires, cones and pinnacles over many millennia. As you explore, immerse yourself in the surreal scenery, and learn how the locals have sculpted homes, churches, villages and underground cities from the rock. Stop for lunch midway and visit the UNESCO-listed Göreme Open-Air Museum, with its fresco-painted rock chapels and monasteries, and Pasabag, where hundreds of fairy chimneys sprout from a valley. Also, see the Castle of Uchisar and descend into Kaymakli Underground City, a maze of passages, chambers and tombs.

Alternatively, take a private tour to a typical Cappadocia stone house to enjoy a traditional, home-cooked meal and experience village life in this age-old region. Afterward, catch your short flight to Istanbul, checking in at your hotel for dinner. Overnight: 4-star Vicenza hotel or similar in Istanbul
Day 8: Istanbul (B)

Check out after breakfast and enjoy a half-day tour of Istanbul. Visit the Grand Bazaar, one of the world’s biggest markets, with more than 4,000 stalls. Roam around and behold the stalls laden with everything from gold, rugs and antiques to ceramics and clothes. Then, visit the 17th-century Egyptian Spice Market. Inhale the heady aromas and marvel at the multi-colored spice, herb, nut and sweet stands. Alternatively, perhaps choose one of the private excursions available. Maybe sample Turkish coffees at a traditional roasting house, or visit a master baklava (filo pastries) shop to taste some sweet treats made in the time-honored way.

After lunch at a local restaurant (own expense), finish your tour with a drop-off at Atatürk Airport or Sabiha Gokcen Airport, Istanbul cruise port, or any centrally located Istanbul hotel where you’re continuing your stay.

title.en: 4-Day Istanbul to Kusadasi Tour Including Gallipoli, Troy, Pergamum and Ephesus

overview: Take in the historic highlights of Turkey’s Aegean Coast as you journey from Istanbul to Kusadasi on this 4-day tour, including 4-star accommodation. Walk the notorious WWI battlefields of Gallipoli and pay your respects to the Turkish and ANZAC troops that lost their lives; see the famous Trojan Horse as you explore the ruins of ancient Troy; and stand in awe before the magnificent Roman theater of Pergamum. Finally, visit UNESCO-listed Ephesus and marvel over the Grand Theater, the Temple of Artemis and the Library of Celsus.
highlights: 4-day trip from Istanbul to Gallipoli, Ephesus, Troy and Pergamum with air- conditioned coach transport
Tour the WWI battlefields at Gallipoli and see ANZAC Cove, the Lone Pine and other memorials
View ancient Troy with its replica wooden horse and learn about its place in Greek myth
See the relics of Pergamum, including its spectacular theater Discover UNESCO-listed
Ephesus on a tour, seeing the Library of Celsus, Temple of Artemis and more
Enjoy 4-star hotel accommodation during two nights in Kusadasi and one night in

Çanakkale Why Our Insiders Chose This Tour If you’re staying in Istanbul and want to spread your sightseeing net wider, this is a brilliantly convenient roundup of Turkey’s top antiquities and Gallipoli peninsula. Plus, it finishes in Kusadasi, so you can stay on afterward for some beach time or to continue exploring on your own.
expect: Your 4-day tour includes guided walking tours of four of Turkey’s historical gems — Gallipoli, Troy, Pergamum and Ephesus — as well as transport by air-conditioned coach from Istanbul and between each site.

Enjoy overnight 4-star hotel accommodation at Çanakkale plus two nights at a 4-star hotel in Kusadasi. Three breakfasts, lunches and dinners, plus pickup from select hotels in Istanbul at the start of your tour are also included. Your tour finishes in Kusadasi on the morning of Day 4.
Itinerary
Day 1: Istanbul – Gallipoli – Çanakkale (L, D)

Start your 4-day tour with a pickup from your hotel in the Sultanahmet or Taksim area of the city, or from central Istanbul. Then, travel by comfortable, air-conditioned coach to the battlefields of Gallipoli.

On route, listen fascinated as your guide gives you the background on Gallipoli — the peninsula where one of WWI’s bloodiest campaigns was waged.The campaign was fiercely resisted by the Ottoman Turks and lasted more than eight months, resulting in thousands of fatalities. Stop for lunch in the area, and in the afternoon, take a Gallipoli walking tour as your guide explains the terrible events that took place here. Visit Australia’s Lone Pine memorial and view the trenches at Johnston’s Jolly and The Nek, a mountain ridge that presided over a failed Australian attack. Stand at ANZAC Cove, where the first landings were made, and see the Chunuk Blair New Zealand Memorial, the site of a heroic New Zealander stand. Afterward, travel across the Dardanelles Strait and check in at your Çanakkale hotel in time for dinner. Overnight: 4-star Iris Hotel or similar in Çanakkale
Day 2: Çanakkale – Troy – Pergamum – Kusadasi (B, L, D)

After breakfast, drive to the UNESCO-listed archaeological site of Troy, believed to be the location of the ancient city that featured in the poet Homer’s work, The Iliad. Explore with your guide as you hear about Troy’s main claim-to-fame: the Trojan War of the 13th or 12th century BC, when after a 10-year siege, the city fell to the Greeks when they smuggled soldiers inside the walls hidden in a giant wooden horse. Hear, too, about the Greek myth of the Trojan prince, Paris, whose flight with Zeus’ daughter, Helen, triggered the war. Ogle the ruins and take photos of the replica wooden horse that symbolizes Troy's famous past. Continue to Pergamum and, after a break for lunch at a local restaurant, tour the remains of this once-powerful Greco-Roman city. Behold the theater, temples and library, and see the Asclepion, the medical school where mud baths, herbal remedies and other strange treatments were meted out in the 2nd and 3rd centuries AD.

After exploring here and time at a leather handicrafts center, travel to your Kusadasi hotel. Check in for two nights, enjoy dinner and spend the evening as you wish. Overnight: 4-star Marina Hotel or similar in Kusadasi
Day 3: Kusadasi – Ephesus – Kusadasi (B, L, D)
Head out after breakfast to enjoy a day of guided sightseeing around UNESCO-listed Ephesus, once the Roman capital of Asia Minor and one of the Mediterranean’s best- preserved ancient cities.

Take a guided walk and gaze in awe at the Library of Celsus and 24,000-seater Grand Theater, where St Paul is said to have preached. Stroll along the colonnaded Arcadian Way where Cleopatra and Mark Anthony once processed in 31 BC, and see other sites such as the Roman bathhouse and Temple of Hadrian.

Stop for lunch in town and visit the ruined Temple of Artemis, built in around 550 BC and once one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. Before returning to Kusadasi, visit a carpet workshop to learn about Turkey’s centuries-old carpet-making tradition. Watch the skilled artisans at work and discover how the different weaving techniques determine the carpets’ values.
Finish your day at Kusadasi, with the evening at leisure and dinner at your hotel. Overnight: 4-star Marina Hotel or similar in Kusadasi
Day 4: Kusadasi (B)
Your 4-day tour ends at your Kusadasi hotel after breakfast, leaving you free to stay on in the town or travel elsewhere independently.

title.en: 2- or 3-Day Cappadocia Tour from Istanbul with Round-Trip Flights

overview: Lose yourself in the fairy-tale landscapes of Cappadocia with this 2- or 3-day taster tour from Istanbul, including round-trip flights and 4-star accommodation in an atmospheric cave hotel. Uncover Cappadocia’s rich history as you tour the UNESCO-listed Göreme Open-Air Museum, explore the underground city of Kaymakli and visit Uchisar Castle. Keep your camera handy as you wander through the bizarre rock formations and fairy chimneys of Pasabag, Devrent and Rose valleys, and learn how the region’s unique topography was sculpted through millions of years of volcanic activity.
highlights: 2-day or 3-day Cappadocia tour from Istanbul with round-trip flights and accommodation included
Fly to Kayseri to explore Cappadocia's awesome rock fairy chimneys, castles and villages
Admire the painted chapels of the UNESCO-listed Göreme Open-Air Museum and climb Uchisar Castle
Marvel at the fairy chimneys of Pasabag and the Devrent Valley
Visit beautiful Rose Valley, Kaymakli Underground City and the pottery town of
Avanos
Choose to stay one or two nights at a 4-star boutique cave hotel
Enjoy a hassle-free trip, with a hotel pickup in Istanbul, plus transport and most meals in Cappadocia included
expect: Experience the best of Turkey’s Cappadocia region on a 2- or 3-day tour, with 4-star accommodation in a cave hotel, return flights between Istanbul and Kayseri, and transport and most meals in Cappadocia included. When you book, you can choose from a 2-day tour with a return to Istanbul late on the second day, or opt for a 3-day tour. With the latter, you stay a second night at your cave hotel, enjoying the evening as you wish and perhaps having dinner (own expense) at the hotel or a restaurant of your choosing. Both the 2-day and 3-day tours include hotel pickup in Istanbul, lunch on both daily tours, plus a return transfer to Kayseri Airport on your way back.
Itinerary
Day 1: Istanbul – Kayseri – Northern Cappadocia (L)

Begin your 2- or 3-day experience with an early morning pickup from your central Istanbul hotel, and travel to Istanbul airport for your flight to Kayseri. Relax on the 1.5-hour flight, and on arrival at Kayseri airport, travel by air-conditioned coach into the heart of Cappadocia. As you travel, hear how this enchanting region was formed during thousands of years of volcanic activity and is rich with strange rock formations, caves and carved stone villages.

Head first for Esentepe, a hillside with spectacular views over the Göreme Valley. Here, take photos of the magnificent, lava-formed landscapes as a taster of what's to come, and then set off with your guide to explore properly.

Visit the rock castle of Uchisar and be wowed by the stunning views from the top. Then, head for the UNESCO-listed Göreme Open-Air Museum, famous for its rock-cut chapels coated in Byzantine frescoes. Admire the beautifully painted chapels and afterward, continue to Ortahisar Castle, another natural castle honeycombed with man-made chambers. Break for a buffet lunch at a local restaurant, and this afternoon, explore two areas known for their mushroom-shaped fairy chimneys. Visit Pasabag (Monk’s Valley), whose chimneys are widely regarded as the best in Cappadocia, and ogle the Devrent Valley, where more mushroom-shaped pinnacles cover the hillsides.
Afterward, drive to your cave hotel and spend the evening at leisure amid Cappadocia’s magical landscapes. Perhaps enjoy dinner (own expense) at your hotel or a nearby restaurant tonight.
Overnight: 4-star MDC Cave Hotel in Cappadocia or a similar standard cave hotel
Day 2: Southern Cappadocia (B, L)

After breakfast, leave your hotel and drive to southern Cappadocia. Stop at Pigeon Valley where over the centuries, locals have carved pigeon houses into the cliffs to collect pigeon manure for use as an agricultural fertilizer.

Walk through Rose Valley, famous for its red-hued rock and hand-cut churches, and visit Kaymakli Underground City, one of Cappadocia’s best-preserved subterranean sites. Delve into the mazy passages and rooms as your guide explains how early Christians used them to hide from persecutors.

Stop for a buffet lunch at a local restaurant, and visit Cavusin, where a now abandoned settlement of rock-cut homes climbs up a hill. Take photos of the eerie village before continuing to the pottery town of Avanos. Watch local potters at work using centuries-old techniques, and perhaps buy some colorful ceramics (own expense) as souvenirs. Later, transfer to Kayseri and fly back to Istanbul where your 2-day tour ends at the airport. Alternatively, if you’ve selected the 3-day tour, return to your cave hotel and spend the evening relaxing as you wish.
Overnight if option selected: 4-star MDC Cave Hotel in Cappadocia or a similar standard cave hotel Optional
Day 3: Cappadocia – Istanbul Airport (B)
Check out after breakfast and transfer to Kayseri airport for your return flight to Istanbul airport, where your tour ends.
